glosses: to determine, to ascertain
to set, to establish

te zullen vaststellen

glosses: bevestigen dat iets zo is

examples.text: Toen de agent bij het ongeluk kwam, kon hij vaststellen dat de auto tegen de lantaarnpaal was gereden.

Het hof zegt niet te hebben kunnen vaststellen dat er in de relatie tussen Bakker en het slachtoffer - met wie hij een verhouding had - een situatie was waarin het meisje werd gedwongen tot seksuele gemeenschap. Dat Bakker in de relatie "erg dominant" was en dat hij misbruik maakte van de kwetsbare situatie waarin het slachtoffer zich bevond, staat volgens het hof buiten kijf.

examples.text: Het vertrek werd vastgesteld op de volgende morgen.

glosses: To strengthen; to make firm or resolute.
To administer the sacrament of confirmation on (someone).

examples.text: She pulled through with the boy till he was confirmed; but then she told him that she could not feed him any longer; he would have to go out and earn his own bread.
Elizabeth, daughter of Henry VIII, was baptized and confirmed at the age of three days.

glosses: To assure the accuracy of previous statements.

examples.text: Despite all the evidence confirming the existence of the Protheans, little is known about their culture and society. From time to time, dig sites will yield new clues, but after 50,000 years of decay, little of value is unearthed.

glosses: To approve a proposal or nomination.

examples.text: The Senate must confirm federal court appointments.

glosses: For sure, definitely.

examples.text: This is confirm not my handwriting.

glosses: To set the boundaries or limits of.

examples.text: [God] hath determined the times before appointed.

glosses: To ascertain definitely; to figure out, find out, or conclude by analyzing, calculating, or investigating.

examples.text: Whether modern, industrial man is less or more warlike than his hunter-gatherer ancestors is impossible to determine. The machine gun is so much more lethal than the bow and arrow that comparisons are meaningless.

glosses: To fix the form or character of; to shape; to prescribe imperatively; to regulate; to settle.

examples.text: The character of the soul is determined by the character of its God.

glosses: To fix the course of; to impel and direct; with a remoter object preceded by to.

examples.text: The news of his father's illness determined him to depart immediately.

glosses: To bring to a conclusion, as a question or controversy; to settle authoritative or judicial sentence; to decide.

examples.text: The court has determined the cause.

glosses: To resolve (to do something); to establish a fixed intention; to cause (something) to come to a conclusion or decision; to lead.

examples.text: I determined to go home at once.

In the same year as the Furness objection, sadder tidings befell St Pancras Priory at Lewes, in East Sussex.
